fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Joseph says the opposite to the cupbearer: “…I have done nothing for which they should have put me in this dungeon.” (Genesis 40:15) He also says he was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews. So the text has Joseph saying he did nothing to earn that dungeon.

Not this time, friend. Verse 3 says Pharaoh imprisoned them in the house of the captain of the guard, “…the same prison where Joseph was confined.” So the king's officers ended up right where Joseph already was. Pharaoh, Egypt's king, was angry with both of them, and that's how they got there.
Cheerful isn't what Joseph saw, friend. Verse 6 says he saw that the two men were distraught. That's why he asks them in the very next verse, “Why are your faces so downcast today?” (Genesis 40:7)

That's what the baker sees. In the top basket are all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh, “…but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.” (Genesis 40:17) Me, I'd be waving my mustache at those birds and hollering. Those baked goods were meant for Pharaoh, and the birds are the ones eating them.

No servants are mentioned in the baker's dream. He says the top basket held all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh, “…but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.” (Genesis 40:17) The birds are the ones doing the eating. The basket is still on his head while it happens.

It's Pharaoh's birthday. Verse 20 says, “On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he held a feast for all his officials…” That's the same three days Joseph had named for both men. A feast for all those officials? My oven timer gets nervous just thinking about it.

That's what the text says. “The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot all about him.” (Genesis 40:23) Joseph had asked him, “…please remember me and show me kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh…” (Genesis 40:14) I think that stings, because Joseph asked so plainly.

That's what Joseph asked for, friend, but it's not what verse 23 says. The cupbearer “…did not remember Joseph; he forgot all about him.” Joseph had asked to be brought out of that prison, and this passage ends with him forgotten. The story isn't over, though.
